name: Philadelphia Experiment
description: An alleged 1943 U.S. Navy experiment said to have rendered the destroyer escort USS Eldridge invisible — and briefly teleported it from Philadelphia to Norfolk — based on Einstein's unified field theory. The story is widely regarded as a hoax originating with letters by Carl M. Allen in 1955–56.
full_description: The Philadelphia Experiment is an alleged event said to have occurred at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard on or around 28 October 1943, in which the U.S. Navy applied an experimental electromagnetic field to the destroyer escort USS Eldridge (DE-173), causing it to become first invisible, then to teleport to Norfolk, Virginia (over 200 miles away), and back, with severe physical and psychological effects on the crew. The story originated in letters sent in 1955–1956 by a merchant mariner named Carl M. Allen (using the pseudonym 'Carlos Miguel Allende') to UFO author Morris K. Jessup, and in heavily annotated copies of Jessup's book 'The Case for the UFO' that were circulated to the U.S. Office of Naval Research. The U.S. Navy and historians have documented numerous fatal problems with the account: USS Eldridge was not commissioned until 27 August 1943; her deck log and war diary show she was not in Philadelphia between August and December 1943; the master of SS Andrew Furuseth (the ship from which Allen claimed to have observed the event) categorically denied any unusual occurrence; and the Office of Naval Research itself was not established until 1946. Allen is reported to have admitted he wrote the annotations 'to scare the hell out of Jessup'. The story was popularized by William Moore and Charles Berlitz's 1979 book 'The Philadelphia Experiment: Project Invisibility' and the 1984 film of the same name, and has become a foundational text of post-WWII secret-experiment conspiracy theory.

aliases.name: Project Rainbow
aliases.meaning: Name used in conspiracy literature for the alleged experiment

origin: The alleged event is associated with two real U.S. locations — the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard, Pennsylvania, and Norfolk, Virginia — but the story has no verified geographic occurrence.

etymology.origin: Named for the alleged location at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard, Pennsylvania.
etymology.meaning: 'The Philadelphia Experiment' as a name was popularized by William Moore and Charles Berlitz in their 1979 book.
etymology.first_use: The story dates to Carl Allen's 1955–56 letters; the title 'The Philadelphia Experiment' was fixed in the public imagination by the 1979 Moore & Berlitz book.

timeline.significance: Pre-dates by ~two months the alleged experiment date; her deck log and war diary establish her actual whereabouts

timeline.event: Date later assigned by conspiracy literature for the alleged invisibility test
timeline.significance: No supporting record exists in Eldridge's deck log or war diary

timeline.significance: Origin of the Philadelphia Experiment narrative

timeline.event: Death of Morris K. Jessup, ruled suicide
timeline.significance: Conspiracy literature later treats this as a suspicious event tied to the experiment
